Q1. Spiral Matrix Traversal

Given an m x n matrix, return all elements of the matrix in spiral order (clockwise starting from top-left).

Constraints

  • m == matrix.length
  • n == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 10
  • -100 <= matrix[i][j] <= 100
Verified Java Solution
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static List spiralOrder(int[][] matrix) {
        List res = new ArrayList<>();
        if (matrix.length == 0) return res;
        int top = 0, bottom = matrix.length - 1, left = 0, right = matrix[0].length - 1;
        while (top <= bottom && left <= right) {
            for (int i = left; i <= right; i++) res.add(matrix[top][i]);
            top++;
            for (int i = top; i <= bottom; i++) res.add(matrix[i][right]);
            right--;
            if (top <= bottom) {
                for (int i = right; i >= left; i--) res.add(matrix[bottom][i]);
                bottom--;
            }
            if (left <= right) {
                for (int i = bottom; i >= top; i--) res.add(matrix[i][left]);
                left++;
            }
        }
        return res;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def spiralOrder(matrix: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    res = []
    while matrix:
        res += matrix.pop(0)
        if matrix and matrix[0]:
            for row in matrix: res.append(row.pop())
        if matrix:
            res += matrix.pop()[::-1]
        if matrix and matrix[0]:
            for row in matrix[::-1]: res.append(row.pop(0))
    return res

Q2. Rotate Image 90 Degrees Clockwise

You are given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image, rotate the image by 90 degrees (clockwise). You have to rotate the image in-place.

Constraints

  • n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= n <= 20
  • -1000 <= matrix[i][j] <= 1000
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static void rotate(int[][] matrix) {
        int n = matrix.length;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
                int temp = matrix[i][j];
                matrix[i][j] = matrix[j][i];
                matrix[j][i] = temp;
            }
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n / 2; j++) {
                int temp = matrix[i][j];
                matrix[i][j] = matrix[i][n - 1 - j];
                matrix[i][n - 1 - j] = temp;
            }
        }
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def rotate(matrix: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
    matrix.reverse()
    for i in range(len(matrix)):
        for j in range(i):
            matrix[i][j], matrix[j][i] = matrix[j][i], matrix[i][j]
    return matrix

Q3. Jump Game

You are given an integer array nums. You are initially positioned at the array's first index, and each element in the array represents your maximum jump length at that position. Return true if you can reach the last index, or false otherwise.

Constraints

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^5
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static boolean canJump(int[] nums) {
        int maxReach = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
            if (i > maxReach) return false;
            maxReach = Math.max(maxReach, i + nums[i]);
            if (maxReach >= nums.length - 1) return true;
        }
        return true;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def canJump(nums: list[int]) -> bool:
    max_reach = 0
    for i, jump in enumerate(nums):
        if i > max_reach: return False
        max_reach = max(max_reach, i + jump)
    return True

Q4. Coin Change

You are given an integer array coins representing coins of different denominations and an integer amount representing a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return -1.

Constraints

  • 1 <= coins.length <= 12
  • 1 <= coins[i] <= 2^31 - 1
  • 0 <= amount <= 10^4
Verified Java Solution
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    public static int coinChange(int[] coins, int amount) {
        int[] dp = new int[amount + 1];
        Arrays.fill(dp, amount + 1);
        dp[0] = 0;
        for (int i = 1; i <= amount; i++) {
            for (int coin : coins) {
                if (coin <= i) dp[i] = Math.min(dp[i], dp[i - coin] + 1);
            }
        }
        return dp[amount] > amount ? -1 : dp[amount];
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def coinChange(coins: list[int], amount: int) -> int:
    dp = [float('inf')] * (amount + 1)
    dp[0] = 0
    for coin in coins:
        for i in range(coin, amount + 1):
            dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i - coin] + 1)
    return dp[amount] if dp[amount] != float('inf') else -1

Q5. Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

Suppose an array of length n sorted in ascending order is rotated between 1 and n times. Given the sorted rotated array nums of unique elements, return the minimum element of this array.

Constraints

  • n == nums.length
  • 1 <= n <= 5000
  • -5000 <= nums[i] <= 5000
  • All the integers of nums are unique.
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static int findMin(int[] nums) {
        int l = 0, r = nums.length - 1;
        while (l < r) {
            int mid = l + (r - l) / 2;
            if (nums[mid] > nums[r]) l = mid + 1;
            else r = mid;
        }
        return nums[l];
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def findMin(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    l, r = 0, len(nums) - 1
    while l < r:
        mid = (l + r) // 2
        if nums[mid] > nums[r]: l = mid + 1
        else: r = mid
    return nums[l]

Q1. Count Inversions in an Array

In an audit data validation pipeline at Deloitte, two numerical audit values a[i] and a[j] are considered inverted if i < j and a[i] > a[j]. Given an array of integers arr, count the total number of inversions in the array.

Constraints

  • 1 <= arr.length <= 10^5
  • 1 <= arr[i] <= 10^9
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static long countInversions(int[] arr) {
        return mergeSortAndCount(arr, 0, arr.length - 1);
    }
    private static long mergeSortAndCount(int[] arr, int l, int r) {
        long count = 0;
        if (l < r) {
            int m = l + (r - l) / 2;
            count += mergeSortAndCount(arr, l, m);
            count += mergeSortAndCount(arr, m + 1, r);
            count += mergeAndCount(arr, l, m, r);
        }
        return count;
    }
    private static long mergeAndCount(int[] arr, int l, int m, int r) {
        int[] left = java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(arr, l, m + 1);
        int[] right = java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(arr, m + 1, r + 1);
        int i = 0, j = 0, k = l;
        long swaps = 0;
        while (i < left.length && j < right.length) {
            if (left[i] <= right[j]) arr[k++] = left[i++];
            else {
                arr[k++] = right[j++];
                swaps += (m + 1) - (l + i);
            }
        }
        while (i < left.length) arr[k++] = left[i++];
        while (j < right.length) arr[k++] = right[j++];
        return swaps;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def countInversions(arr):
    def merge_count(arr):
        if len(arr) <= 1:
            return arr, 0
        mid = len(arr) // 2
        left, left_inv = merge_count(arr[:mid])
        right, right_inv = merge_count(arr[mid:])
        merged, split_inv = [], 0
        i = j = 0
        while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
            if left[i] <= right[j]:
                merged.append(left[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(right[j])
                split_inv += len(left) - i
                j += 1
        merged.extend(left[i:])
        merged.extend(right[j:])
        return merged, left_inv + right_inv + split_inv
    _, count = merge_count(arr)
    return count

Q2. Group Anagrams

Deloitte Tax analysts process client financial item descriptions that contain scrambled ledger keys. Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together into sublists. You can return the answer in any order.

Constraints

  • 1 <= strs.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= strs[i].length <= 100
  • strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
Verified Java Solution
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static List> groupAnagrams(String[] strs) {
        Map> map = new HashMap<>();
        for (String s : strs) {
            char[] chars = s.toCharArray();
            Arrays.sort(chars);
            String key = new String(chars);
            map.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(s);
        }
        return new ArrayList<>(map.values());
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
from collections import defaultdict
def groupAnagrams(strs):
    ans = defaultdict(list)
    for s in strs:
        ans[tuple(sorted(s))].append(s)
    return list(ans.values())

Q3. Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

Given a string s representing client audit session tokens, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

Constraints

  • 0 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4
  • s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.
Verified Java Solution
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static int lengthOfLongestSubstring(String s) {
        Map map = new HashMap<>();
        int maxLen = 0, left = 0;
        for (int right = 0; right < s.length(); right++) {
            char c = s.charAt(right);
            if (map.containsKey(c)) {
                left = Math.max(left, map.get(c) + 1);
            }
            map.put(c, right);
            maxLen = Math.max(maxLen, right - left + 1);
        }
        return maxLen;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def lengthOfLongestSubstring(s: str) -> int:
    used = {}
    max_len = start = 0
    for i, c in enumerate(s):
        if c in used and start <= used[c]:
            start = used[c] + 1
        else:
            max_len = max(max_len, i - start + 1)
        used[c] = i
    return max_len

Q4. Trapping Rain Water

Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

Constraints

  • n == height.length
  • 1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4
  • 0 <= height[i] <= 10^5
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static int trap(int[] height) {
        int left = 0, right = height.length - 1;
        int maxLeft = 0, maxRight = 0, res = 0;
        while (left <= right) {
            if (height[left] <= height[right]) {
                if (height[left] >= maxLeft) maxLeft = height[left];
                else res += maxLeft - height[left];
                left++;
            } else {
                if (height[right] >= maxRight) maxRight = height[right];
                else res += maxRight - height[right];
                right--;
            }
        }
        return res;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def trap(height: list[int]) -> int:
    left, right = 0, len(height) - 1
    max_left = max_right = res = 0
    while left <= right:
        if height[left] <= height[right]:
            if height[left] >= max_left: max_left = height[left]
            else: res += max_left - height[left]
            left += 1
        else:
            if height[right] >= max_right: max_right = height[right]
            else: res += max_right - height[right]
            right -= 1
    return res

Q5. Subarray Sum Equals K

Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of continuous subarrays whose sum equals to k.

Constraints

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 2 * 10^4
  • -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000
  • -10^7 <= k <= 10^7
Verified Java Solution
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static int subarraySum(int[] nums, int k) {
        Map map = new HashMap<>();
        map.put(0, 1);
        int sum = 0, count = 0;
        for (int n : nums) {
            sum += n;
            if (map.containsKey(sum - k)) count += map.get(sum - k);
            map.put(sum, map.getOrDefault(sum, 0) + 1);
        }
        return count;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
from collections import defaultdict
def subarraySum(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    count = 0
    curr_sum = 0
    prefix = defaultdict(int)
    prefix[0] = 1
    for n in nums:
        curr_sum += n
        count += prefix[curr_sum - k]
        prefix[curr_sum] += 1
    return count

Q1. Product of Array Except Self

In an EY GDS financial portfolio analyzer, each asset index requires computing the product of all other assets without using the division operator. Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].

Constraints

  • 2 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • -30 <= nums[i] <= 30
  • The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static int[] productExceptSelf(int[] nums) {
        int n = nums.length;
        int[] ans = new int[n];
        ans[0] = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) ans[i] = ans[i - 1] * nums[i - 1];
        int r = 1;
        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            ans[i] = ans[i] * r;
            r *= nums[i];
        }
        return ans;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def productExceptSelf(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(nums)
    res = [1] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        res[i] = res[i - 1] * nums[i - 1]
    r = 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        res[i] *= r
        r *= nums[i]
    return res

Q2. Set Matrix Zeroes

Given an m x n integer matrix matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0s in-place.

Constraints

  • m == matrix.length
  • n == matrix[0].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 200
  • -2^31 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2^31 - 1
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static void setZeroes(int[][] matrix) {
        boolean col0 = false;
        int rows = matrix.length, cols = matrix[0].length;
        for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
            if (matrix[i][0] == 0) col0 = true;
            for (int j = 1; j < cols; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] == 0) matrix[i][0] = matrix[0][j] = 0;
            }
        }
        for (int i = rows - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            for (int j = cols - 1; j >= 1; j--) {
                if (matrix[i][0] == 0 || matrix[0][j] == 0) matrix[i][j] = 0;
            }
            if (col0) matrix[i][0] = 0;
        }
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def setZeroes(matrix: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
    col0 = False
    rows, cols = len(matrix), len(matrix[0])
    for i in range(rows):
        if matrix[i][0] == 0: col0 = True
        for j in range(1, cols):
            if matrix[i][j] == 0:
                matrix[i][0] = matrix[0][j] = 0
    for i in range(rows - 1, -1, -1):
        for j in range(cols - 1, 0, -1):
            if matrix[i][0] == 0 or matrix[0][j] == 0:
                matrix[i][j] = 0
        if col0: matrix[i][0] = 0
    return matrix

Q3. Excel Sheet Column Number

Given a string columnTitle that represents the column title as appears in an Excel sheet, return its corresponding column number.

Constraints

  • 1 <= columnTitle.length <= 7
  • columnTitle consists only of uppercase English letters.
  • columnTitle is in the range ["A", "FXSHRXW"].
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static int titleToNumber(String columnTitle) {
        int ans = 0;
        for (char c : columnTitle.toCharArray()) {
            ans = ans * 26 + (c - 'A' + 1);
        }
        return ans;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def titleToNumber(columnTitle: str) -> int:
    ans = 0
    for c in columnTitle:
        ans = ans * 26 + (ord(c) - ord('A') + 1)
    return ans

Q4. Happy Number

Write an algorithm to determine if a number n is happy. A happy number is a number defined by the following process: Starting with any positive integer, replace the number by the sum of the squares of its digits, and repeat until the number equals 1 or loops endlessly.

Constraints

  • 1 <= n <= 2^31 - 1
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static boolean isHappy(int n) {
        int slow = n, fast = getNext(n);
        while (fast != 1 && slow != fast) {
            slow = getNext(slow);
            fast = getNext(getNext(fast));
        }
        return fast == 1;
    }
    private static int getNext(int n) {
        int sum = 0;
        while (n > 0) {
            int d = n % 10;
            sum += d * d;
            n /= 10;
        }
        return sum;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def isHappy(n: int) -> bool:
    def get_next(num):
        return sum(int(d)**2 for d in str(num))
    slow = n
    fast = get_next(n)
    while fast != 1 and slow != fast:
        slow = get_next(slow)
        fast = get_next(get_next(fast))
    return fast == 1

Q5. Power of Two

Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two. Otherwise, return false. An integer n is a power of two, if there exists an integer x such that n == 2^x.

Constraints

  • -2^31 <= n <= 2^31 - 1
Verified Java Solution
public class Solution {
    public static boolean isPowerOfTwo(int n) {
        return n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0;
    }
}
Verified Python Solution
def isPowerOfTwo(n: int) -> bool:
    return n > 0 and (n & (n - 1)) == 0

Accenture On-Campus Hiring — Recruitment Process

Stage

Round

No

Recruitment Flow

Registration / Application → Behavioral & Cognitive Assessment → Technical Assessment → Coding Assessment → Communication Assessment → Technical + HR Interview → Final Selection / Offer

Role

Approx. CTC

Selection Context

Associate Software Engineer (ASE)

₹4.5 LPA

Standard fresher technology role

Advanced Associate Software Engineer (AASE)

₹6.5 LPA

Higher-performing candidates / advanced track

Advanced Application Engineer (AEH)

~₹11–12 LPA

Premium technology track; availability depends on the hiring drive

1. Registration / Application

Candidates register through the applicable Accenture campus hiring process and submit the required academic, personal, and application details.

2. Behavioral & Cognitive Assessment

This assessment evaluates behavioral traits and cognitive problem-solving ability. The reported 2026 campus pattern includes a behavioral questionnaire followed by gamified cognitive tasks such as path finding, mathematical problem solving, and key-and-door navigation.

Reported Pattern: 54 behavioral questions followed by gamified cognitive tasks.

3. Technical Assessment

The Technical Assessment evaluates fundamental technical and programming knowledge through multiple-choice questions.

Reported Pattern: 45 questions · 45 minutes

Reported Areas: Pseudocode, programming logic, Operating Systems, Computer Networks, Network Security, MS Office fundamentals, and code/output-based questions.

4. Coding Assessment

The Coding Assessment evaluates programming, database, and frontend development skills through three problems.

Reported Pattern: 3 questions · 60 minutes

Problem

Area

Reported Technologies

1

Backend / DSA

Java, Python, or C#

2

Database

SQL

3

Frontend / Web Development

HTML, CSS, JavaScript

The exact programming language options may vary by assessment version.

5. Communication Assessment

Candidates who clear the required assessment stages proceed to a Communication Assessment designed to evaluate their English communication ability.

Reported Areas: Speaking, listening, pronunciation, fluency, grammar, vocabulary, and sentence construction.

The exact format and duration can vary by hiring drive.

6. Technical + HR Interview

Candidates who successfully clear the assessment stages are shortlisted for the interview.

The interview may combine technical and HR/behavioral evaluation rather than functioning as two completely separate interviews.

Technical

Questions may cover programming fundamentals, Object-Oriented Programming, Java, Python, C/C++, SQL, DBMS, Operating Systems, Computer Networks, Data Structures, and technologies mentioned on the candidate's resume.

Coding / Problem Solving

Candidates may be asked to solve or explain programming problems involving basic DSA, programming logic, arrays, strings, searching, sorting, or SQL.

Project / Resume

Candidates may be questioned about their projects, internships, certifications, technologies, responsibilities, implementation decisions, challenges, and solutions.

Candidates should be prepared to explain everything mentioned on their resume.

Behavioral / HR

Questions may cover:

  • Tell me about yourself

  • Why Accenture?

  • Strengths and weaknesses

  • Career goals

  • Teamwork and leadership

  • Handling challenges

  • Relocation and work preferences

  • Career motivation

7. Final Selection / Offer

Candidates who successfully clear the required assessment and interview stages move to the final selection stage. Selected candidates receive the applicable offer/joining communication from Accenture.

Important Note

This represents the reported 2026 Accenture on-campus pattern. Accenture's assessment content and process can vary by hiring drive and role, so exact question counts, timings, and assessment components should be treated as reported current patterns rather than permanent company-wide specifications.

Q1. Rat Count House

A student volunteer is organizing a community food drive to supply grain packets to a colony of rats living along a residential street. There are r rats in the colony, and each rat requires unit amount of food to be completely satisfied. The street consists of n houses arranged in a row, where the i-th house contains arr[i] units of food.

The student collects food sequentially starting from house 0 and visits houses one by one in order. Determine the minimum number of houses the student must visit to collect enough food to satisfy all the rats. If the total food available across all houses is insufficient to meet the overall demand, return -1. If the input array is empty or null, return 0.

Constraints

  • 1 <= r, unit <= 100
  • 0 <= n <= 1000
  • 1 <= arr[i] <= 100

r = 7, unit = 2, n = 8

Q2. Binary String Operations

A computer science student is building an expression evaluator for a logical circuit simulation. The circuit receives an input string str consisting of binary digits ('0' and '1') separated by uppercase alphabetic operator characters. The character 'A' denotes bitwise AND, 'B' denotes bitwise OR, and 'C' denotes bitwise XOR.

The student evaluates the expression strictly from left to right without applying standard mathematical operator precedence. For instance, given the expression "1C0C1C1A0B1", the student first evaluates 1 XOR 0 to get 1, then 1 XOR 1 to get 0, and continues sequentially until the final result is computed. Write a program to evaluate the string and return the final binary result. If the input string is empty or null, return -1.

Constraints

  • 1 <= str.length <= 10^5
  • The string starts and alternates between binary digits ('0', '1') and uppercase operator characters ('A', 'B', 'C').

Q3. Password Security Validator

An intern is designing a security verification utility for a university student portal. The system must inspect a student's proposed password string str and determine whether it complies with all institutional security standards.

A valid password must satisfy five strict conditions: it must be at least 4 characters long, contain at least one numeric digit from '0' to '9', contain at least one uppercase letter from 'A' to 'Z', must not contain any spaces or forward slashes ('/'), and its first character must not be a digit. Return 1 if the password meets all security rules, or 0 if it violates any rule.

Constraints

  • 0 <= n <= 10^5
  • Characters can be any standard printable ASCII characters

Q4. Elements Within Difference Threshold

During a laboratory experiment, a student records a sequence of sensor measurements stored in an integer array arr of size n. The student needs to calibrate the apparatus against a reference baseline value num under an allowable margin of error diff.

A sensor measurement is considered acceptable if the absolute difference between the measurement and the baseline value is less than or equal to diff. Write a function to count how many elements in the array fall within this acceptable tolerance. If no elements meet this condition, return -1.

Q5. Difference of Divisible and Non-Divisible Sums

A mathematics student challenges their peers with a numerical puzzle involving a divisor n and an upper bound m. The student analyzes all integers in the inclusive range from 1 to m and divides them into two categories based on their divisibility by n.

The student computes sum1 as the sum of all integers between 1 and m that are not divisible by n, and sum2 as the sum of all integers between 1 and m that are divisible by n. Your task is to calculate and return the difference obtained by subtracting sum2 from sum1.

Q6. Large Small Sum

A student is participating in a coding competition where they must analyze an integer array arr of size n based on index positions. The student splits the array conceptually into two subsets: elements located at even indices (0, 2, 4, ...) and elements located at odd indices (1, 3, 5, ...).

From the even-indexed elements, the student identifies the second largest value. From the odd-indexed elements, the student identifies the second smallest value. Return the sum of the second largest element at even positions and the second smallest element at odd positions. If the array has 3 or fewer elements, or is null, return 0.

A student shopper holds a promotional gift coupon with a maximum budget of sum and wants to purchase two distinct items from a catalog represented by an integer array arr of size n.

Among all eligible pairs, the student selects the pair with the smallest sum. If multiple pairs share the same minimum sum, the student selects the pair yielding the smallest product. A student formatting an administrative dataset notices that product serial numbers contain hyphens placed haphazardly across strings. To standardize the format, the student wants to rearrange each string by relocating all hyphen characters ('-') to the very beginning.

All remaining alphanumeric characters must preserve their original relative order without any alterations. For example, when given the string "Move-Hyphens-to-Front", the reformatted output should be "---MoveHyphenstoFront". If the input string is empty or null, return null.

A teaching assistant is creating a tutoring application to help elementary school students master column-by-column addition. To gauge difficulty, the assistant wants to know how many carry operations are generated when adding two positive integers num1 and num2.

Q14. Autobiographical Number

A student exploring recreational mathematics investigates autobiographical numbers. An autobiographical number is a non-negative integer string where the digit at index 0 indicates the total count of zeros in the number, the digit at index 1 indicates the count of ones, the digit at index 2 indicates the count of twos, and so on. For example, "1210" is autobiographical because it contains one 0, two 1s, one 2, and zero 3s.

Write a function to check whether a given numeric string is autobiographical. If the number is autobiographical, return the count of distinct digits appearing in the string (for "1210", the distinct digits are '0', '1', and '2', so the result is 3). If the string is not autobiographical, return 0.

A student organizing a raffle assigns numbered tickets across an inclusive interval [lower, upper]. The student wants to identify how many ticket numbers are palindromic, meaning they read identically in both forward and backward directions.

All single-digit numbers from 1 to 9 are naturally palindromic, while multi-digit numbers such as 11, 88, 101, and 121 are also palindromic. Write a function that returns the total count of palindromic integers within the range [lower, upper].

Q16. Subarray Product Less Than K

A financial software trainee is designing an algorithm to flag contiguous transaction intervals where the compounded risk factor, calculated as the product of transaction values, stays strictly below a risk threshold k.

Given an array of positive integers nums of size n and an integer ceiling k, write a function to count the total number of contiguous subarrays where the product of all elements in the subarray is strictly less than k. Q17. Superior Elements

A business analytics student is evaluating monthly sales records stored sequentially in an integer array arr of size n. The student wants to identify all standout months, termed superior elements, where sales exceeded every subsequent month in the fiscal cycle.

An element is considered superior if it is strictly greater than all the elements appearing to its right in the array. Q18. Count Inversions in Array

A student benchmark analyst is measuring how unsorted an array arr of size n is by calculating its inversion count. The inversion count reflects how many swap operations a comparison-based algorithm would perform to arrange the array into ascending order.

Formally, two elements arr[i] and arr[j] form an inversion if they satisfy the condition i < j while arr[i] > arr[j]. If the array is already sorted in non-decreasing order, the inversion count is 0. If the array is sorted in descending order, the inversion count reaches its maximum possible value. Write a function to calculate and return the total number of inversions in the array.

However, a logistics mismatch occurred, causing exactly one serial number to appear an odd number of times. All other numbers appear an even number of times. Write a function to identify and return the unique serial number that occurs an odd number of times.

Q21. Minimum Steps to Make Product Equal to One

A student developing a turn-based number game needs an algorithm to calculate the minimum cost required to transform an integer array arr of size n. In each step, the student can either increment any element by 1 or decrement any element by 1.

The objective is to modify the array such that the product of all elements equals exactly 1, while keeping the total number of modification steps as low as possible. Write a function that calculates and returns the minimum number of steps required to achieve this product.

The student wants to identify the most successful continuous trading period by finding the contiguous subarray that yields the largest possible sum. The subarray must contain at least one element. Write a program to determine and return the maximum contiguous subarray sum.

Q23. Array Equilibrium Index

A structural engineering student modeling the weight distribution of a suspension bridge needs to find a balance point along a sequence of measured section loads stored in arr of size n.

An index i is called an equilibrium point if the sum of all elements strictly to the left of index i is equal to the sum of all elements strictly to the right of index i. For boundary elements, the sum of elements outside the array boundary is taken as 0. Return the first 0-based equilibrium index found in the array. If no equilibrium point exists, return -1.

  • -10^5 <= arr[i] <= 10^5

Q24. Anagram String Verification

A linguistics student developing an educational word game needs a validator to determine whether two submitted lowercase words, str1 and str2, are anagrams of each other.

Two strings are anagrams if they contain the exact same characters with identical frequencies, differing only in the arrangement of the letters. For example, "listen" and "silent" are anagrams because rearranging the characters of one produces the other. Return 1 if the two strings are valid anagrams, otherwise return 0.

Q25. Next Greater Element to Right

A student creating an automated price alert system needs to inspect a sequence of daily stock values arr of size n and determine the next upcoming market peak for each day.

For every element in the array, the task is to find the first element situated to its right that has a strictly greater value. If no greater element exists to the right of a given element, its next greater value should be designated as -1. Print or return the next greater element for each position separated by a space.

Q26. Permutations of Consonants

A student researching combinatorial language patterns wants to find how many unique word variations can be formed from a given string str by rearranging only its consonant letters.

The vowels in the string are 'A', 'E', 'I', 'O', 'U' and their lowercase equivalents. All remaining alphabetic letters are consonants. Q27. Digital Root

A mathematics student is studying recursive reduction methods and wants to automate the calculation of the digital root for a given positive integer n.

The digital root is computed by taking the sum of all individual digits of n. If the resulting sum is 10 or greater, the process of summing the digits is repeated recursively until a single-digit integer between 1 and 9 is obtained. Write a function that returns this final single-digit result.

A robotics engineering student processing a 2D sensor grid needs to calculate the cumulative intensity along the diagonals of an n x n square matrix.

The student must calculate the sum of all elements situated along the primary diagonal (from top-left to bottom-right) combined with all elements situated along the secondary diagonal (from top-right to bottom-left). If the dimension n is odd, the element located at the exact intersection of both diagonals must be counted only once. Write a program to compute this combined diagonal sum.

  • 1 <= mat[i][j] <= 1000

Q29. Longest Common Prefix

A software developer trainee building a predictive search engine needs to determine the longest prefix shared across an array arr of n search query strings.

The function must examine all strings in the array and return the longest common sequence of characters that appears at the very beginning of every single string. If there is no common prefix shared among all strings, return "-1".

Q30. Trapping Rain Water

An architecture student simulating urban rainwater drainage is analyzing an elevation profile represented by a non-negative integer array height of size n. Each element height[i] denotes the height of a building block whose base width is 1 unit.

After a heavy rainfall, water accumulates in the hollows formed between taller structures. Write a function that computes the total volume of trapped rainwater that can be retained within the elevation map.

Q31. Missing Number in Sequence

A university exam invigilator is cataloging student roll numbers submitted after an examination. The examination room was assigned n students with consecutive roll numbers ranging from 1 to n inclusive. However, after collection, the invigilator notices that exactly one student's answer booklet is missing, leaving only n - 1 roll numbers recorded in the array arr.

All numbers present in the array are distinct and lie within the range from 1 to n. Write a function to identify and return the single missing roll number from the sequence.

Constraints

  • 2 <= n <= 10^5
  • arr.length == n - 1
  • 1 <= arr[i] <= n
  • All elements in arr are distinct
🧪 Test Cases

Q32. Pairs with Target Difference

A data science student analyzing correlations in a temperature dataset needs to count how many pairs of readings exhibit a specific variance. The student is given an integer array arr of size n and a non-negative target difference diff.

The student must find and count all pairs of indices (i, j) with i < j such that the absolute difference between their values equals diff, meaning |arr[i] - arr[j]| == diff. Write a function that calculates and returns the total count of such valid pairs.

Constraints

  • 2 <= n <= 10^5
  • 0 <= diff <= 10^9
  • -10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9

3

0

Input: 
n = 4, diff = 0

2

Q33. Run Length String Compression

A telecommunications student is developing a lossless data compression algorithm for transmitting repetitive alphanumeric text sequences. The compression format, known as run-length encoding, replaces consecutive identical characters with the character followed immediately by the count of its consecutive repetitions.

For example, when compressing the string "aabbbcccc", the algorithm encodes two 'a's as "a2", three 'b's as "b3", and four 'c's as "c4", resulting in "a2b3c4". Write a program that takes an input string str consisting of alphabetic characters and returns its compressed run-length encoded representation.

Constraints

  • 1 <= str.length <= 10^5
  • str consists of lowercase and uppercase English letters
🧪 Test Cases
Test Case 1
Input: 
str = "aabbbcccc"
Output: 
a2b3c4
Test Case 2
Input: 
str = "abcd"
Output: 
a1b1c1d1
Test Case 3
Input: 
str = "aaaaa"
Output: 
a5

Q34. Second Most Frequent Character

A cryptanalysis student studying monoalphabetic substitution ciphers is analyzing character frequency distributions in intercepted messages. The student needs an automated tool to identify the character that appears with the second highest frequency in a given string str.

The function must determine the frequency of each distinct character in the string. The character with the second highest occurrence count should be returned. If all characters in the string occur with the exact same frequency, or if no unique second most frequent character exists, the function should return "-1".

Constraints

  • 1 <= str.length <= 10^5
  • str consists of lowercase English alphabets
🧪 Test Cases
Test Case 1
Input:

b

Input:

c

-1

Q35. Maximum Product Subarray

An investment analytics student evaluating portfolio growth rates wants to identify the most explosive compounding period from a sequence of daily multiplying factors stored in an integer array nums of size n.

The student needs to locate a contiguous non-empty subarray within nums that produces the largest possible product when all its elements are multiplied together. The array may contain positive integers, negative integers, and zeros. Write a program to compute and return this maximum subarray product.

Constraints

  • 1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4
  • -10 <= nums[i] <= 10
  • The product of any prefix or suffix of nums fits within a 64-bit integer

Q36. Majority Element

A campus election committee representative is verifying ballot votes recorded in an integer array nums of size n, where each number represents a candidate identifier. The election rules declare that a candidate is elected outright if they secure a strict majority of all cast votes.

A majority element is defined as a candidate ID that appears strictly more than n / 2 times in the array. Write a function that finds and returns the majority element. If no candidate has received more than half of the total votes, the function should return -1.

Constraints

  • 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

-1

n = 1

99

Q37. Intersection of Two Sorted Arrays

A university registrar is cross-referencing attendance lists from two different advanced seminars. The participant student IDs for the first seminar are stored in a sorted array arr1 of size n, and the IDs for the second seminar are stored in a sorted array arr2 of size m.

Both arrays are sorted in non-decreasing order and may contain duplicate entries. The registrar wants to generate a list containing all unique student IDs that appear in both attendance sheets. Print the common unique elements in ascending order separated by a single space. If there are no common attendees, output "-1".

Constraints

  • 1 <= n, m <= 10^5
  • 1 <= arr1[i], arr2[j] <= 10^9
  • Both arr1 and arr2 are sorted in ascending order

Q38. Vowel to Consonant Substrings

A computational linguistics student investigating phonological patterns in text strings is studying transition boundaries between vowels and consonants. The student wants to count how many contiguous substrings within a lowercase English string str begin with a vowel and terminate with a consonant.

The vowels in the alphabet are 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', and 'u', while all other twenty-one letters are consonants. A valid substring can be of any length greater than or equal to 2, provided its first character is a vowel and its final character is a consonant. Write a function to calculate and return the total count of such valid substrings.

Constraints

  • 1 <= str.length <= 10^5
  • str consists solely of lowercase English alphabetic characters

1

Q39. Wave Array Arrangement

A digital signal processing student wants to convert a sorted sequence of amplitude readings arr of size n into an alternating wave pattern. In a wave array, the elements alternate such that the first element is greater than or equal to the second, the second is less than or equal to the third, the third is greater than or equal to the fourth, and so on: arr[0] >= arr[1] <= arr[2] >= arr[3] <= arr[4]...

The input array is already sorted in ascending order. The student can achieve the lexicographically smallest wave form by swapping every consecutive pair of adjacent elements starting from index 0. Rearrange the array in-place and output the resulting wave sequence separated by spaces.

Constraints

  • 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 1 <= arr[i] <= 10^9

Q40. Count Pairs with Given Sum

A chemistry student preparing standardized test solutions needs to combine pairs of chemical vials from an inventory of n vials, where each vial i has a concentration of arr[i]. The experimental procedure requires the combined concentration of the two combined vials to match a target concentration k exactly.

The student needs to count how many distinct index pairs (i, j) with i < j satisfy the condition arr[i] + arr[j] == k. Write a function that computes and returns the total number of such compatible vial pairs.

  • 1 <= k <= 10^9

Q41. Rotate Array by K Positions

A systems engineering student designing a circular task scheduling buffer needs a utility to shift an array of process identifiers arr of size n to the right by k positions.

When an element shifts past the last index of the array, it wraps around to the beginning. For example, shifting the array [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] to the right by 3 positions causes the last 3 elements to wrap around to the front, yielding [5, 6, 7, 1, 2, 3, 4]. Write a program that rotates the array to the right by k steps and returns or prints the rotated sequence separated by spaces.

Constraints

  • 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 0 <= k <= 10^9
  • -10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9

1 2 3

Q42. Check for Armstrong Number

A mathematics student researching special integer properties wants to verify whether a given positive integer num is an Armstrong number, also known as a narcissistic number.

A positive integer containing d digits is classified as an Armstrong number if the sum of each of its individual digits raised to the power of d equals the number itself. For instance, 153 has 3 digits, and 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3 = 1 + 125 + 27 = 153, making it an Armstrong number. Write a function that returns 1 if num is an Armstrong number, and 0 otherwise.

Constraints

  • 1 <= num <= 10^9
🧪 Test Cases
Test Case 1
Input: 
num = 153
Output: 
1
Test Case 2
Input: 
num = 120
Output: 
0
Test Case 3
Input: 
num = 370
Output: 
1

Q43. Search in a 2D Sorted Matrix

A database student implementing a two-dimensional indexing structure stores key records inside an n x m matrix mat. The matrix possesses the property that every individual row is sorted in ascending order from left to right, and every individual column is sorted in ascending order from top to bottom.

The student needs to determine whether a target value x exists anywhere within the matrix. If the target integer x is present within the matrix, the search function should return 1. If the target does not exist in the matrix, the function should return 0.

Q44. Longest Consecutive Sequence

A logistics coordinator tracking package dispatch records is given an unsorted array of integer day timestamps arr of size n. The coordinator wants to discover the length of the longest streak of consecutive days during which packages were continuously dispatched.

The consecutive elements do not need to appear contiguously in the original array, but when ordered numerical values are considered, they must form an uninterrupted sequence of integers with step 1. Write an algorithm that finds and returns the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence. If the array is empty, return 0.

Q45. Roman to Integer Conversion

A history student digitizing inscriptions on ancient architectural ruins is transcribing monument completion dates written in Roman numerals. The numerals use seven standard symbols with fixed values: 'I' represents 1, 'V' represents 5, 'X' represents 10, 'L' represents 50, 'C' represents 100, 'D' represents 500, and 'M' represents 1000.

Numerals are typically written from largest to smallest from left to right. However, when a smaller numeral precedes a larger numeral, subtraction is applied (such as IV representing 4, IX representing 9, XL representing 40, XC representing 90, CD representing 400, and CM representing 900). Write a program to convert an input Roman numeral string s into its equivalent base-10 decimal integer.

  • 1 <= s.length <= 15
  • s contains only the characters 'I', 'V', 'X', 'L', 'C', 'D', 'M'

Input:

9

A school teacher has n packets of chocolates where each packet contains a certain number of chocolates represented in an array arr. The teacher wants to distribute exactly m packets among m children attending a classroom celebration so that every child receives exactly one packet. To keep the distribution as fair as possible, the teacher must select m packets such that the difference between the maximum number of chocolates in a chosen packet and the minimum number of chocolates in a chosen packet is minimized.

A geography student is surveying an elevation path across n terrain stations recorded in an array nums. A terrain station is considered a peak element if its elevation is strictly greater than the elevations of its immediate neighbors. For boundary stations at the start and end of the array, a station is considered higher than nonexistent external territory. If the terrain possesses multiple peak points, identifying the index of any valid peak element is acceptable.

A software engineering student is building a syntax highlighter that parses mathematical expressions containing bracket characters in an input string s. The allowed bracket characters include round parentheses, curly braces, and square brackets.
